messages:
chloe (AE): Hey team — running a POC for AcmeCorp right now. They saw a bunch of 5xxs during a ramp test at ~11:08 PT. Can we swarm? They’re worried about SLA for the upcoming exec demo.
jamal (SE): On it. Do we have request IDs or region? Is this hosted or dedicated POC?
chloe (AE): Hosted, us-west1. Devon (customer) pasted a few request ids in the deal thread, pulling them into here: rId=acme-20260321-1, acme-20260321-2.
devon (customer): Yep — those are the ones. Test script was hitting 40 RPS with bursts to 120 for ~30s. Repro steps in their script: 
```
for i in {1..1000}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"lorem"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
done
```
chloe (AE): Their plan is to demo tomorrow — we need a mitigation path quick.
alex (SRE): Pasting the short logs we grabbed from the request stream: 
```
[2026-03-21T18:08:12Z] rId=acme-20260321-1 status=503 code=backlog_exceeded queue_depth=512 max_q=500
[2026-03-21T18:08:13Z] rId=acme-20260321-2 status=502 code=kernal_oom host=gpu-11
```
Looks like queue backlog + a kernel OOM on one host. Autoscaler-bot triggered a scale event but there’s a lag.
jamal (SE): Queue depth 512 > 500 threshold. Autoscale delay is expected during sharp bursts. Can we confirm the autoscaler logs? @autoscaler-bot any details?
autoscaler-bot: scale_event: triggered=true reason=queue_depth threshold=500 current=512 target_replicas=6 scaling_start=2026-03-21T18:08:14Z estimated_ready=2026-03-21T18:09:05Z
maria (Eng): The estimated_ready time matches what we saw — ~50s spin-up on that pool. That's too slow for demo bursts. Two immediate mitigations: 1) enable short-term fallback routing to a smaller model variant (lower memory) 2) route bursts to a warm burstpool (if enabled) or increase min_replicas.
jamal (SE): For hosted customers we can enable model fallback on the routing policy: `fallback: [redwood-medium, redwood-small]` which avoids kernel oom on the heavy host. Also set `min_replicas: 3` for the current pool to keep a baseline.
chloe (AE): Can we flip fallback and bump min_replicas now for Acme POC? What's the risk to cost?
alex (SRE): Risk is extra cost for baseline GPU hours; small for a 24h demo window. I can bump `min_replicas` to 3 for the pool and enable the fallback policy for their customer-id. Will do in 2m and report.
jamal (SE): Also ask the customer to add an Authorization header retry strategy and client-side pacing: small jittered backoff for 429/5xx. That reduces simultaneous inflight requests.
devon (customer): We can add jitter. But curious — why did the OOM happen? They were using redwood-large model the whole time.
maria (Eng): redwood-large has higher memory and higher single-host kernel sensitivity. Under bursty concurrent sequences the KV cache and concurrency cause transient kernel OOMs. Fallback to redwood-medium avoids the heavy kernels.
alex (SRE): Update: I bumped min_replicas and enabled fallback to redwood-medium. Also spun up a temporary burstpool (warm instances). Scaling log: 
```
[autoscaler] set min_replicas=3 for pool acme-pool
[burstpool] warm_instances=4 state=ready
```
Retry your burst test please and drop the first two request ids if possible — we cleared the queued requests.
devon (customer): Rerunning now (starting at 11:12 PT). Will report in ~90s.
jamal (SE): While they rerun, can someone check if our routing policy used slow regional fallback instead of model fallback? We saw a handful of requests routed to eu-west && failed.
maria (Eng): Looks like routing tried region fallback due to a previous policy rule `prefer_region:true`. I recommend a temporary override `prefer_region:false` for this customer so model fallback kicks in first.
alex (SRE): Override applied. Also collecting more detailed host logs for the OOM: `/var/log/redwood/hosts/gpu-11/oom.log` snapshot attached to ticket.
jamal (SE): If we keep seeing kernel OOMs even with fallback, we'll need to repro with a captive workload and adjust kernel memory tunables or pin to different instance types.
chloe (AE): Devon — if this run looks clean can you confirm the lowest-latency percentile for the demo traffic? They want p50 < 120ms.
devon (customer): First run looks much better. I see a few 503s at start but then stable. p50 ~85ms, p95 ~420ms (those are the tail spikes).
amber (AE): @chloe — tagging for post-demo follow-up: recommend ops changes: increase baseline, enable burstpool for demos, and set model fallback by default for POCs.
jamal (SE): Action items I’ll take: 1) add a quick runbook snippet for POC ramps 2) add sample client-side backoff code 3) open engineering ticket to reduce autoscale spin-up time.
maria (Eng): I’ll file the engineering ticket: `INF-6482 reduce autoscaler cold spinup latency`. Add logs and reproducer.
alex (SRE): Closing loop: monitoring alert thresholds adjusted to queue_depth=400 for POC cohorts and we’ll run a small chaos test tomorrow.
devon (customer): Thanks team — demo looks viable now. Appreciate the fast turnaround :thumbsup:
chloe (AE): Great work, all. I’ll update the deal thread and schedule a 30m retro with Acme after the demo.
